s4a_3h_4h_plateau_analysis.observation: rl[3h]=rl[4h]=10 despite 30-min boredom timer creating temporal spread
s4a_3h_4h_plateau_analysis.root_cause: Both the 3h window (since 02:06Z) and 4h window (since 01:06Z) cover a span that includes all 7 boredom goal types at least once. Goal[5] at 03:43Z ('check substrate health...') dispatches substrate-health-tick, producing substrateHealthReport in the 3h window — the same shape that goal[1] at 01:43Z produces in the 4h-exclusive slice. No unique shape in 4h that isn't already in 3h.
s4a_3h_4h_plateau_analysis.path_to_resolution: Either (1) add-resolver-to-vessel or other n=0 templates fire with unique output_shapes, or (2) new templates get registered and execute within the 4h-window exclusive slice but not in the 3h window, or (3) goal cycle diversification so adjacent windows have genuinely different shape coverage.
s4a_3h_4h_plateau_analysis.prediction_retraction: Investigation-027 prediction (via 3d27f632 substrate commit) of first coverage_progress=True at ~04:11-04:43Z was not realized. The 3h/4h plateau is a structural blocker not addressed by the 30-min timer alone.

next_wake_recommendation.rationale: S.4a plateau at 3h/4h is structural — short-interval checks add no information until add-resolver-to-vessel or a new unique-shape template fires. Next full boredom cycle completes at ~08:13Z (goal[6] fires again). Checking at 06:30Z gives the 1h window (06:30–05:30Z) two more boredom firings to observe. 5400s (1.5h) balances cache overhead against information gain.
what_to_look_for: Has rl[4h] > rl[3h]? (plateau broken → consecutive can reach 3)
Has add-resolver-to-vessel alpha grown above 1? (new template firing)
